## 2. Symptom (observable) + reproducibility profile
- **HLK (Windows Hardware Lab Kit \u2014 Microsoft's HW certification suite)** **"Connected Standby IO Stress"** (8 hr, Driver Verifier on) fails with **"Multiple BSOD"** `[confirmed]`.
- Bugchecks observed: **`UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION (0x154)`** and **`KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR (0x7A)`** `[confirmed, Comment 3]`. **No dumps generated** — storage not responding at failure.
- **Earliest capture was a HANG, not a clean BSOD:** GDHM dump `3235882136` (2025-12-12) is a **forced/debugger-break dump** (`BUGCHECK_CODE 0`) of a hung system — GDHM's “Bsod / `0x0_nt!SwapContext`” label is only the capture mechanism (analyzed via bsod-copilot `BSOD0xE2-guide.md`; see §5f). So the failure presents as **both** timeout/hang dumps **and** the 0x154/0x7A clean bugchecks.
- Failure lands **during S0ix entry or exit**; OS recovery succeeds a few times, then a later recovery fails → **soft hang or bugcheck** `[confirmed, Comment 10]`.
- **Heisenbug:** with **WinDbg attached, passes 3/3**, no dumps collectible; one soft-hang seen after detaching `[confirmed, Comments 3–5]`.
- **Reproducibility gates (all [confirmed], Comment 10):**
  - UFS = **primary** storage (NVMe-primary + UFS-secondary → **no repro**).
  - **Windows 25H2** only (24H2 clean).
  - Clean OS **+ Gfx + Wifi** drivers installed (clean OS alone → no CS asserted → no repro).
  - Failure rate **100%** in the failing HLK config (ticket header).

## 3. Initial triage — first discriminators
- **Rule-in (it IS this):** HLK CS IO-stress on **UFS-primary / Win25H2**; a SCSI command — a **READ(06)** (`SRB.TimeOutValue = 0xa`) *or*, on the enumeration path, an **INQUIRY** — hits a **10 s unit-timeout**; FTH/VISA show the command **never reached the UFS IP**; OS runs a **hierarchical reset** (`storufs!UfsResetBus` → `storport!RaidAdapterResetBus`); recovery **fails on the SK hynix** device.
- **Rule-out (it is NOT this) — state the exact condition:**
  - Needs PKGC? **NO** — repros with **PKGC disabled** `[confirmed, Comment 10 #5]`. **← key discriminator vs Pattern P1 (`ufs-fabric-timeout-on-pkgc`, 16027585017), which is PKGC-gated.**
  - Boot-time PMC-stuck / IP_ready? **NO** — not a boot/fuse-pull hang → **not P2** (`ufs-fusepull-cdc-race-on-boot`, 16029205689).
  - UFS PHY **signal marginality**? **NO** — repros at **0 dB, −3.5 dB, −6 dB** CTLE equalization `[confirmed, Comment 9]`. *(This ruled out PHY **signal-integrity** as the trigger — distinct from the M-PHY **link-startup** failure seen during recovery (`DME_LINKSTARTUP` PHY err `0x10`, §5g/§7), which is real; eq-tuning does not fix the ~10 s no-response.)*
  - UFS PGCB sequencing? **NO** — repros with PMC PGCB WA at **20 ms / 30 ms** `[confirmed, Comment 9]`.
  - Link-gear marginality? **NO** — repros at **Gear 3** as well as Gear 4 `[confirmed, Comment 10 #6]`.
  - UFS HW hang? **NO** — UFS resumes normally after the eng-driver breakpoint releases `[confirmed, Comment 11]`.
  - Known **LPSS / bugcheck-`0x9F`** issue? **NO** — removing the **LPSS driver** (to rule out the known `9F` UFS issue) still repros (`0x154`); one setup also **hung at `01CS` post code** `[confirmed, Comment 3]`.
- **Nearest look-alike:** P1 — same platform/UFS-primary/S0ix surface and the same `storufs!UfsResetBus` OS reset path, but **P1 needs PKGC and shows `IS_` SBFES/HBFES OCP-fabric errors**, whereas this repros PKGC-off with the transaction **lost above PSF0 and no fabric error**. **Deciding tell:** PKGC-disabled still fails **and** VISA@PSF4/PSF0 shows **no** UFS-side transaction/error.

## 4. Reproduction recipe (config, images, IFWI, knobs, operating point)
- **Board:** WCL DDR5 SODIMM T3 RVP1. **BKC:** `WCL-25H2-CONS-PROD-25.49.3.16`.
- **IFWI:** `WILDCATLAKEN.0.WCLN.2025.49.2.01` (A1). **BIOS:** `WCL_BIOS_3463_04`. **FSP:** `02.01.025.4750`.
- **UFS devices:** SK hynix **HN8T15DEHKX075** (256 GB) — **fails**; Samsung **KLUEG8UHGC-B0E1** — **recovers**.
- **OS:** Windows **25H2** `26200.7309`; **Gfx + Wifi drivers installed**; **UFS = primary**.
- **Test:** HLK **Connected Standby IO Stress**, Driver Verifier on, 8 hr — three concurrent workloads:
  - **RapidFileVerify** (1M file, Read/Verify enabled),
  - **ConnectedStandby** (random dwell 3/10/25/30/60/75/300/3000 s),
  - **SCSICompliance** (Inquiry, TestUnitReady, RequestSense, Read6/10/16, ReadCapacity10/16, StartStopUnit, SynchronizeCache10, ModeSense6/10, ModeSelect6/10, Reserve6/10, Release6/10).
- **Expect:** during an S0ix transition a SCSI READ times out (10 s) → OS recovery → after a few successful recoveries a **soft hang / BSOD**.
- **Mitigation to avoid repro:** none clean pre-fix; the MSFT private driver (§8) removes the soft hang.

## 5. Fault evidence & instrumentation (machine-readable evidence map)
> Capture/decode procedure for every log below lives in the `unified-ufs-log-analysis` skill
> (`bsod-dump.md`, `driver-etl.md`). The findings here are specific to this sighting.


### 5a. WinDbg — OS reset path `[confirmed, Comments 8 & 11]`
| command / namednode | field | value @ fault | inference | rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dt SRB _SCSI_REQUEST_BLOCK` | `+0x014 TimeOutValue` | `0xa` (10 s) | SCSI **READ(06)**, QueueTag `0x03` unit-timeout | decisive |
| `kv` stack | call site | `storufs!UfsIntelLkfResetBus → UfsResetBus → storport!RaCallMiniportResetBus → RaidAdapterResetBus → RaidUnitHierarchicalReset → RaidHierarchicalResetWorkRoutine → nt!IopProcessWorkItem` | OS ran full **multi-tier reset** (LUN → abort → device → **bus reset**) | decisive |
| dump `16029462685_UFS` | type | **breakpoint** (eng driver), not a bugcheck | failure caught **at UFS reset**, not a HW fault | useful |

> **Recovery-sequence note `[confirmed, Comment 11]`:** the **abort uses the same SRB → inherits the same 10 s timeout**, so a failing abort just burns another 10 s before escalating. And the OS cannot simply toggle HCE and ring the doorbell — **every HCE toggle must follow `LSS (Link Startup) → PMC to HS-G4 / PWM-G1 → data transfer`** before any new transaction; the driver waits for that reset+link-startup to complete before restarting IO (link state is outside the OS). *(Comment 11 states this as a general OS-recovery principle — it does not mention Samsung/SK hynix or link-up/link-lost at all. The claim that this specific sequencing requirement is "why SK hynix derails" is msure's separate hedged hypothesis from comment `1667271550` — see §5d/§7 — not something Comment 11 itself confirms.)*

### 5c. VISA `[confirmed, Comment 10 #2]`
- At failure, **no transaction pending in UFS**; confirmed at **PSF4** and **PSF0** → the READ is **lost above PSF0** (D2D boundary or compute die). Basis for **Issue #1** — later root-caused to the **UFS `FeatureFlags` (`UTRLCNR`+Auto-Hibernate)** completion-method; the missed `UTRLCNR` completion (link auto-hibernated) explains the "no completion seen" observation (§7, `15019125953` comment [20]). A **P2SB HW bug** (`14025696732`) was also listed by the debugger as a possible cause of IO timeouts in general, but was **not confirmed applicable to this specific loss**.

**Snap→vendor (confirmed):** `comment_1667271550.png` = **Samsung** (In[20]/In[29]); `comment_1667271550_1.png` = **SK hynix** (In[41]/In[42]).

|---|---|---|---|
| `HCS.DP` (0) | Device Present | **0** — link lost | **1** — link up |

| `IS_.UDEPRI` (1) | UIC DME_ENDPOINTRESET Indication | flags the endpoint reset | flags the endpoint reset |

> UniPro Section 8.2.6 & 8.2.2 — HCE is toggled"* (comment `1667271550`) — not a traced/confirmed mechanism.

### 5f. Hang dump — bsod-copilot / `BSOD0xE2-guide.md` (GDHM 3235882136) `[confirmed, Log.txt + comment.txt]`
Earliest capture (2025-12-12, ~35 min uptime). Decode method: see `unified-ufs-log-analysis/knowledge/bsod-dump.md` (`0xE2` forced-hang methodology). Findings:
| probe | observed | inference | rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!analyze -v` | **`BUGCHECK_CODE: 0`** (`ERROR_CODE 0x80000003` breakpoint), bucket `0x0_nt!SwapContext` | **not a bugcheck** — a **forced dump of a HANG** over a connected debugger (bugcheck = capture mechanism, per 0xE2) | decisive |
| `!pnptriage` thread | System PnP device-action worker blocked **~22.06s** (`Ticks 1412`): `KeWaitForSingleObject → storport!RaidBusEnumeratorIssueSynchronousRequest → GenericInquiry → VisitUnit → RaidAdapterEnumerateBus → RescanBus → QueryDeviceRelationsIrp → PnpDeviceActionWorker` | a bus-rescan **INQUIRY** to the UFS unit never completes → PnP worker wedged | decisive |
| `!irp` (pended) | `IRP_MJ_PNP / IRP_MN_QUERY_DEVICE_RELATIONS` on `\Driver\storufs` | OS is re-enumerating the UFS bus when it wedges | decisive |
| `!devnode` | `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_4D47` ServiceName `storufs`, State **`DeviceNodeEnumeratePending`**, StateHistory **flapping** `Started(0x30a)↔EnumerateCompletion(0x30f)↔EnumeratePending(0x30e)` | UFS devnode in a **re-enumeration loop** (corroborates repeated D0/D3 recovery) | high |
| victim thread | second System thread blocked `ExpWaitForResource → CmpLockRegistry` (registry lock); many pending **wait-wake S0/S4** power IRPs | the enumeration wedge **cascades** → registry/PnP/power pile up → whole-system hang | high |
> **Interpretation:** the **enumeration-path** face of the same fault — a synchronous request to the UFS
> device (here the PnP **INQUIRY**, not a SCSI READ) hangs because the device/link won't answer, wedging
> PnP and cascading to a system hang. Directly analogous to the 0xE2 guide's **USB4 D-state ping-pong**
> (device D3→D0 flapping) + **PPM gate-stall** (one worker wedged, others pile up). It's the earliest
> evidence face (pre-dates the eng-driver-breakpoint SCSI-READ captures) and explains the generic
> `0x0_nt!SwapContext` “timeout” hang bucket. Provenance: GDHM `3235882136`; not attached to HSD.
>
> **Reproduced (2nd hang dump, 2025-12-22, comment 1667202197):** same wedge (~**29.5s**; devnode
> started→enumerate-pending window ~**7 min**), plus two discriminators: (1) at the hang the UFS devnode is
> **PowerDeviceD0** and `!storadapter`=**Working** → **rules out power-gate/D3** (device is *on*, just won't
> answer the INQUIRY); (2) the stall reaches the **filesystem** — an NTFS USN-journal worker
> (`Ntfs!NtfsCheckUsnTimeOutWorker → ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite`) is blocked behind it. Two captures 10
> days apart ⇒ **repeatable signature**, not a one-off.

### 5g. Storport RaidLogList + UIC/M-PHY link-startup failure `[confirmed, ticket 16029462685 / nithyapr]`
Extracted (via `!storloglist` + the storufs UIC command log) from the eng-driver-breakpoint dumps on the
**promoted IP-debug ticket 16029462685**. Two decisive pieces:
| probe | observed | inference | rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!storloglist` (RaidLogList) | `UnitTimeOut` → `RESET LUN [Error]` → `RESET DEVICE [Error]` → `PauseAdapter (Timeout 30)` → `Bus reset`; aborted SRB = **`SCSI READ(10)`** (enum path: `SCSI INQUIRY`) | a SCSI cmd got **no HW response for ~10 s** → OS **hierarchical reset** (LUN/DEVICE fail → Bus reset) | decisive |
| UIC cmd trace (Bus reset) | `DME_SET`(MIB `0x155e0000`)→Success; **`DME_LINKSTARTUP` ×5 → `[HW Error][PHY][ErrorCode 0x10]` → Failure**; **`DME_ENDPOINTRESET` → Failure** (`IS=0x45724877`) | during recovery the **M-PHY link won't re-init** (PHY error 0x10) — concrete reason enumeration/recovery stalls | decisive |
| Dec-12 dump storlog | `SCSI/INQUIRY 07:50:21 → UnitTimeOut 07:50:31` (10 s) | same ~10 s no-response pattern on the enumeration path | high |
> **MSFT's verdict on the link-startup failure `[confirmed, origin 14026588381 / sibling 15019125953 comment 9]`:** the **`DME_LINKSTARTUP ×5 / PHY ErrorCode 0x10`** rows above are **MSFT's own `[Reset Bus]` UIC trace** (not an Intel-generated one). MSFT's read of it: *“the UFS link is in a bad state at the time of failure. Recovery flow seems to be failing really early during the link startup stage. **I am not sure if this state is even software recoverable**, if even link startup is failing… this issue should be looked into from the **UFS hardware perspective** by Intel.”* So the link-re-init failure was first flagged as a possible **HW/device** problem — which is what steered the debug toward the vendor-device angle (§7, Issue #2).
> **Analyst conclusion (nithyapr, 16029462685):** *“This is **not a bugcheck**… link was active and SCSI READ
> was smooth (HW responding within ~1 ms), then one SCSI READ hung and UnitTimeout hit → OS hierarchical
> reset… the reason behind the OS reset is **no response for a SCSI command for ~10 second**, so we have to
> **check from HW side** why it hung… breakpoint hit **6 times**, pattern same → the underlying issue is there
> in the normal case and **recovering without our notice.”*  Provenance: GDHM 3235882136 /
> `\\amr.corp.intel.com\wos\EXT\Friday\16029462685`. See `driver-etl.md` for the storport/UIC log signature.

## 6. Debug flow (diagnostic narrowing)
1. **Early HW-hang hypothesis + reproduction gates found (Comment 7):** initial theory was *"UFS flash doesn't respond to UFS bus reset."* A clean-OS-from-ISO baseline did **not** repro — but only because Connected Standby isn't asserted without the **Gfx + Wifi drivers** installed, not because anything was fixed. This is what established the **reproduction gates** later confirmed in §2 (UFS-primary, Win 25H2, Gfx/Wifi drivers).
2. **Known-bug rule-out (Comment 3):** pulled the **LPSS driver** to rule out a known UFS/LPSS bugcheck-`0x9F` issue — still repros (now `0x154`/`0x7A`); one run even hung at the `01CS` POST code.
3. **PHY/PGCB sweep (Comment 9):** swept CTLE eq (0/−3.5/−6 dB) and PMC PGCB WA (20/30 ms) → still repro → ruled out PHY signal-integrity and PGCB sequencing as the *trigger*.
4. **Reproducibility gates nailed down (Comment 10):** confirmed repros with **PKGC disabled** — the key discriminator that rules out look-alike Pattern P1 (§3) — and at **Gear 3** as well as Gear 4 (rules out link-gear marginality); FTH + VISA@PSF4/PSF0 show **no txn at UFS, none pending** → the command is lost *above* PSF0.
5. **Device hung? (Comment 11):** eng-driver breakpoint at UFS reset; UFS resumes fine after release → **not a HW hang** — this **contradicts the Comment-7 hypothesis** — the problem is a **lost SCSI command**, not an unresponsive device (§5a/§5b).
6. **Where is the command lost, and why (sibling ticket `15019125953`)?** root-caused to the UFS **`FeatureFlags`** combination (`UTRLCNR` completion-notification + Auto-Hibernate) → **Issue #1**; fixed via doorbell-completion default `0x11` (25H2'7D) (§5c, §7, comment [20]).
7. **Why hang, not retry?** On timeout OS runs a **hierarchical reset**; for **SK hynix**, Endpoint Reset leaves **link up / `IS_` clean / `DP=1`** — per msure's own hedged hypothesis (§7), this steers OS onto a path that skips the HCE-toggle → link never re-inits → recovery **spins the UTRLDBR/UTRLCLR loop** (§5b) → **soft hang** → **Issue #2**.
8. **Confirm vendor dependency (§5d):** Samsung sets **`IS_.DFES` + link-lost (`DP=0`)** → OS HCE-toggles → recovers. Difference is the device's reaction to Endpoint Reset → **spec-implementation gap**.
9. **Fix probe (Comment 13):** the working MSFT **private driver skipped the Device Reset step entirely** (the step carrying the illegal `DME_ENABLE`), so recovery falls through to **Bus Reset's already-existing HCE toggle** → **soft hang no longer reproduces** on Samsung **or** SK hynix (§8). *(Note: the HCE toggle is pre-existing in Bus Reset — not something MSFT added; Intel's original ask had been phrased as "add an HCE toggle," but the delivered fix was skipping Device Reset.)*
10. **Deeper dump analysis (promoted ticket `16029462685`):** across the forced hang dumps and the eng-driver-breakpoint captures, storport `!storloglist` + the UIC log pin the mechanism — trigger = a SCSI cmd with **no HW response ~10 s** → hierarchical reset → bus reset → **`DME_LINKSTARTUP` fails, PHY err `0x10`** (link won't re-init). The hang dumps, read from the OS-kernel side (bsod-copilot, §5f), show the enumeration INQUIRY wedging the PnP worker — the same fault's enumeration-path face. The eng-driver breakpoint hit **6×**, **silently recovering** each time in normal operation (§5f/§5g). This reframes step 1's early "SW flow" framing into **"config-driven trigger + vendor-dependent recovery gap."**
11. **Side finding, not part of the root-cause chain (Comment 14):** HLK **kit regression** — Kit `26100.6584` fails (24H2 **and** 25H2), Kit `26100.4484` passes — escalated to MSFT separately.
12. **Disposition (Comment 16):** sighting closed, RC'd as **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and OS**.

## 7. Root cause (precise mechanism + class)
- **Two problems, chained:** Issue #1 is a config bug that makes a SCSI command (READ or INQUIRY) time out after ~10 s. Issue #2 is a vendor-dependent gap in how Windows recovers from that timeout, which turns it into a soft hang — but only on SK hynix. Fixing either one independently stops the user-visible hang; both are fixed.
- **Issue #1 — unit-timeout `[ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED]`:** UFS `FeatureFlags` bitmap bit `0x01` (Auto-Hibernate) + bit `0x10` (I/O-completion method). With the completion bit **clear**, the driver uses the completion-notification register (`UTRLCNR`); combined with Auto-Hibernate (link auto-enters H8), the completion is missed → the ~10 s unit-timeout. It self-recovers silently in normal operation (eng-driver breakpoint hit **6×**, same pattern) — the visible HLK hang is only the rare tail. **Fix:** default the bitmap to **`0x11`** from **25H2'7D**, so completions go via the **doorbell register (`UTRLDBR`)** instead — *"in this case we don't hit this timeout problem … not seen with 25H2'7D"* (`15019125953` comment [20]). This **refines** the earlier *"READ lost above PSF0"* hypothesis (§5c): the loss maps to the missed `UTRLCNR` completion, not an unexplained fabric drop. Interim: **errata #288262** (valid to Aug 31 2026).
  - *P2SB note:* that same comment also names a **P2SB HW bug** (`14025696732`, a separate ticket) as one of **two possible** causes of UFS IO timeouts in general. Only the FeatureFlags mechanism above is confirmed and fixed in this thread — the P2SB bug is **unconfirmed** here and not folded into this root cause.
- **Issue #2 — recovery soft-hang `[ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED]`:** UFS device reaction to `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` differs by vendor — **SK hynix** returns **link-up + `IS_` clean** (`DP=1`); **Samsung** returns **link-lost + `IS_.DFES` set** (§5d). This **differing response to `DME_ENDPOINTRESET`** is the confirmed root cause (closing comments 15/16: *“Response to Endpoint Reset is different between Samsung & SKHynix”* → *“spec implementation gap between Vendor devices and OS”*). Samsung's error flag drives Windows onto the recovery path that **HCE-toggles and re-inits the link** → recovers. SK hynix's silence is believed to drive it onto a path that **skips that re-init** — this specific branch logic is **msure's own hedged hypothesis** (*"perhaps this sets driver on a certain path of recovery … perhaps as per UniPro §8.2.6/§8.2.2"*, comment `1667271550`), **never traced directly in code or logs**. What **is** directly confirmed, independent of that hypothesis: during the resulting bus-reset escalation, **MSFT's `[Reset Bus]` UIC trace** shows **`DME_LINKSTARTUP` failing 5× with a PHY hardware error (`0x10`)** and **`DME_ENDPOINTRESET` failing** — the M-PHY/UniPro link will not re-initialize, which is the concrete mechanism by which recovery stalls into the `UTRLDBR`/`UTRLCLR` spin (§5b) → soft hang (§5g). **MSFT's own early read was that this link-startup failure might be a device/HW problem — *“not sure if this state is even software recoverable”* — which is why the vendor-device reaction, not a pure SW reset bug, became the focus.** Contributing protocol smell in FTH: the recovery path also issues **`DME_ENABLE` (UICCMD `0x39`)**, which the IP databook says is **not permitted** `[fth-snap]`. **Fix:** the working private driver **skips the Device Reset step entirely** (per Sajin/MSFT, comment `1667271568`: "we skipped the device reset similar to the LUN reset") — avoiding the illegal `DME_ENABLE` Device Reset used to send — and funnels straight to **Bus Reset**, which already performs a proper HCE toggle before `DME_LINKSTARTUP`; soft hang no longer reproduces on **either** vendor. The fix working on both vendors is the real evidence behind msure's hypothesis; the exact branch logic itself was never independently traced. → **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and the OS recovery flow.**
- **root_cause_class:** Issue #1 → **config/spec** (UFS `FeatureFlags` completion-method; fix = doorbell-completion default). Issue #2 → **spec-gap** (Intel-specific reset path vs OS generic flow / vendor-implementation gap; fix in the OS driver). The P2SB HW bug (`14025696732`) is an **unconfirmed alternate possibility**, not folded into either classification.

### 7b. Fingerprint registers (high level)
- **`HCS.DP` (bit 0)** — `0` Samsung (link lost) vs `1` SK hynix (link retained): the branch selector for the OS recovery path.
- **`IS_.DFES` (bit 11)** — **set on Samsung, clear on SK hynix** after Endpoint Reset: the presence/absence of the fatal-error status is what routes the OS onto the recovering vs hanging path.
- **`IS_.UDEPRI` (bit 1)** — flags the `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` event.
- **`UTRLDBR` (0x58) / `UTRLCLR` (0x5C)** — the doorbell/clear pair the recovery loop pounds.
- **`UICCMD` (0x90) = 0x39 (DME_ENABLE)** — the databook-prohibited command seen during recovery.
- Full bit-level decode (offsets, access, enable bits, spec text) → add to `reference/ufs-glossary.md` and link here.

## 8. Fix & verification (or workaround + status)
- **Actual PV-unblock disposition (origin bug 14026588381 fields):** a **Manual errata `#288262`, valid till Aug 31 2026**, was provided to **unblock the HLK/WHCK test** — explicitly *“not a fix but an errata to unblock PV; Intel still needs to debug and fix the unit-timeout issue for future platforms.”* `workaround_type=temporary`, `fixed_in_version=Manual errata #288262`, `closed_reason=3rd_party`; **closed by pakumars 2026-02-15 (ww08)**. Note: **`#288262` is a separate manual errata**, *not* the cloned errata-writeup `13014563592` (which never finalized — see §10).
- **Issue #2 (engineering fix):** **MSFT private/eng driver** — per Sajin (MSFT)'s own note (comment `1667271568`): *"In the binary that I provided to you which shows good results, **we skipped the device reset similar to the LUN reset**."* Device Reset was the step that sent the illegal `DME_ENABLE` and was hardcoded to always report failure anyway; skipping it funnels straight into **Bus Reset**, which already does a proper **HCE toggle** (`UfsStopAdapter`→`UfsHostControllerEnable`) before `DME_LINKSTARTUP`/`DME_ENDPOINTRESET` — avoiding the illegal command entirely. **Result:** original soft hang not reproduced on **both** Samsung & SK hynix in HLK `[confirmed, Comment 13]`. *(Intel's original ASK to MSFT, comment `1667271550`, was phrased as "insert an HCE toggle after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET`/`DME_RESET`" — that's the recommendation, not what Comment 13 confirms was actually tested/working.)*
  - **Productization:** under MSFT discussion — they may accept only a **smaller interim change**; tied to the current **“2x2”** driver ask. An **ACPI-based variant** was discussed (Klein) but “does not exist today in any of our platforms.”
  - **Productization status (correlated, latest — origin bug `14026588381` comments 19–21):** MSFT checked in the WCL stability fixes targeting the **Ge 8D LCU**, rolled out via the **CFR process (not fully enabled in 8D)**; as of the last update (Jun 2026) Intel still had to **validate EEAP drops to confirm effectiveness**. The **errata `#288262` was extended +90 days** because the 8D-via-CFR timing risked the Aug-2026 waiver expiry. The Issue-#1 tracker's later summary (`15019125953` comment 20) states the reset-flow fix is **“part of 25H2'8D CFR”** (Intel-specific path removed → generic). Net: **landed and rolling out via CFR, await-verify — not a one-shot “shipped.”**
- **Issue #1 [ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED]:** unit-timeout root-caused to **UFS `FeatureFlags` `UTRLCNR`+Auto-Hibernate**; **fixed** by the **doorbell-completion default `0x11` from 25H2'7D** ("not seen with 25H2'7D"). Interim **errata #288262** (to Aug 31 2026). SK hynix vendor behavior was also engaged (WW8.2'2026) during debug. Status `implemented/await-verify` = awaiting confirmation it stays clean on 25H2'7D. *(P2SB bug `14025696732` was listed as an alternate possible cause, not confirmed applicable — see §7.)*
- **HLK kit regression [`comment [14]`]:** Kit `26100.6584` fails (24H2 **and** 25H2), Kit `26100.4484` passes — tracked via clone to `pltf_win_os` (`16029462685`); escalated to MSFT.
- **Disposition:** sighting `rnavinku` **closed** RC'd as **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and OS** `[confirmed, Comment 16]`; origin platform bug closed **`complete / workaround`** via the manual errata (`sysdebug_forum`: “WW07 MSFT provided manual errata, closing as known errata”).
- **This sighting's own HLK unblock (comment 15):** besides the errata, msure cited a **CSS waiver to MSFT, ticket `16029798734`** — **no unit-timeout was seen on the N-1 HLK kit**, so the failing test was waived while Issue #1 debug continued from the HW side.

## 9. Retrospective (avoidable? prevention? detection gap?)
- **Dead-ends / false leads (do not rechase):** UFS PHY CTLE eq, PMC PGCB WA, link gear (G3), "UFS HW hung", and **PKGC** (repros disabled) — all disproven (§3).
  - **"UFS flash doesn't respond to UFS bus reset"** (early HW hypothesis, Comment 7) — **contradicted** by Comment 11: UFS resumes fine after the breakpoint releases, so the device is not stuck; the lost READ never reached UFS in the first place.
  - **Known LPSS / `0x9F`** issue — ruled out by removing the LPSS driver; still repros (Comment 3).
  - **Clean OS-from-ISO baseline** (Comment 7) — no repro, but only because CS isn't asserted without Gfx/Wifi drivers; not a fix, just confirms the trigger needs the driver stack.
- **Detection gap:** only surfaces on **Win 25H2** + **UFS-primary** + **Gfx/Wifi drivers** + the exact HLK concurrency (RapidFileVerify + CS + SCSICompliance); clean-OS and manual inbox-driver mimics did **not** repro → put this **specific concurrency** in the default validation matrix.
- **Prevention:** validate **vendor-device Endpoint-Reset behavior** (link-lost + `IS_.DFES` vs link-up + clean) against the OS recovery flow **before** qualifying a new UFS device; ensure the recovery path does not get stuck in a reset tier (e.g. the Intel-specific Device Reset carrying the illegal `DME_ENABLE`) that fails to re-init the link before escalating.
- **Observability trap:** WinDbg-attached masks it; use the eng-driver breakpoint at UFS reset to force a usable dump.

## 12. Debug story

Picture a laptop (WCL-U) that boots Windows from a UFS flash chip — a SK hynix part. Run Microsoft's HLK "Connected Standby IO Stress" certification test on it and, after a while, it blue-screens. But only in a very specific setup: **Windows 25H2** (24H2 is fine), **UFS as the *primary* drive** (swap in an NVMe as primary and the problem vanishes), and the **graphics + Wi-Fi drivers installed** so the machine actually drops into deep sleep. Frustratingly, the instant you attach a debugger to catch it, it stops failing.

The team burned through a lot of dead ends first — worth knowing so nobody repeats them. They pulled the LPSS driver to rule out a *known* UFS bug: still failed. They suspected the flash chip was simply dead and not answering. To test that, Microsoft supplied a special engineering driver that **halts the system at a debugger breakpoint the instant the UFS reset begins** — freezing everything right at the suspected point of failure so it can be examined. When the engineers then **let execution continue from that breakpoint, the UFS chip resumed normally and answered later commands** — something a genuinely hung or dead device could never do. So the hardware wasn't broken: a command had gone *missing*, the chip hadn't died.

They also went after the usual hardware suspects one by one, and every door closed. They **tuned the UFS PHY's signal equalization** — the electrical fine-tuning (CTLE) that compensates for a weak or noisy link — sweeping it from the default 0 dB through −3.5 dB and −6 dB, in case the physical signal was marginal; it **still failed** at every setting. They **adjusted the power-gating sequence timing** — the PMC "PGCB" workaround, tried at both 20 ms and 30 ms — in case the UFS block was being powered down or woken slightly out of sequence; **still failed**. They **slowed the link from its top speed (Gear 4) down to Gear 3**, in case the high-speed link itself was marginal; **still failed**. And they **turned deep sleep (PKGC) off entirely**, in case entering the deepest package low-power state was the trigger; it *still* failed. Taken together, these ruled out the whole "it's a UFS hardware, electrical, or power-state problem" family and pointed instead at something in the **software/flow** — which is exactly where the root cause turned out to live. The PKGC result carried a second payload: an earlier, similar-looking bug (16027585017) only reproduces *with* deep sleep **on**, so "still fails with PKGC off" cleanly ruled out that cousin as well.

The breakthrough came from a special engineering driver that **halts the system the instant the UFS reset begins** — capturing a clean dump at the moment of failure, unlike the earlier forced dumps of an already-frozen system, which were caught too late to show the lead-up. Read with plain WinDbg, that dump showed a single disk **read** command sitting for **10 seconds** and timing out, with FTH and VISA traces proving the read **never even reached the UFS chip**. Tellingly, the breakpoint caught the **exact same pattern six separate times, and every time the system quietly recovered on its own** — so in normal use the platform rides straight through this and you’d never notice; the HLK stress test just happens to catch the rare time recovery fails.

*Why* that read goes missing was pinned down separately, on the Issue-#1 tracker. Two explanations were floated — a separately-tracked P2SB hardware bug, or a **UFS configuration flag** — and only the second was verified. The flag controls how the driver detects a completed transfer; the leading explanation is that signalling completions through the “notification” register (`UTRLCNR`) while the link is allowed to auto-sleep (Auto-Hibernate) lets a completion slip by unseen, so the command times out. The fix was to switch the default so completions go through the **doorbell register** instead (flag value `0x11`), from **25H2'7D** — and with that, the timeout no longer happens. (The P2SB bug was never confirmed as the actual cause here — a different ticket, named only as one of two things that *can* cause this class of timeout.)

But the timeout is only the *trigger*. The hang comes from **how Windows tries to recover**. On a timeout, Windows runs the same escalating reset for every device — LUN Reset (a no-op in Intel's driver), then Device Reset, then Bus Reset — and the Device-Reset and Bus-Reset tiers each issue a **`DME_ENDPOINTRESET`** to the UFS device. **The two vendors' devices react to that Endpoint Reset differently, and that is the confirmed root cause of the hang:** Samsung **drops the link** (`DP=0`, `IS_.DFES` set), while SK hynix **keeps the link reporting “up”** (`DP=1`, no error). Both then reach Bus Reset's `DME_LINKSTARTUP`, but the outcome differs: with Samsung's clean link-down, link-startup re-establishes from a known state and recovers; with SK hynix's link still “up,” **`DME_LINKSTARTUP` fails five times with a PHY hardware error (`0x10`)** and the link won't come back. Microsoft looked at this first and wasn't even sure it was fixable in software — *“I am not sure if this state is even software recoverable… look into from the UFS hardware perspective”* — which is exactly why the investigation turned to the device-vendor behavior rather than a pure driver bug. The fix, in the end, was a driver change that **skips the broken Device Reset step entirely** (it was issuing an illegal `DME_ENABLE` and always failing anyway), so recovery goes straight to Bus Reset's clean HCE-toggle + link-startup. With that, the hang stopped on **both** vendors. Why exactly that is enough to recover SK hynix was never spelled out in the thread — the evidence is simply that it works on both.

The **earlier forced hang dumps** — the ones caught on an already-frozen system — show this recovery failure from a second angle: not the storage driver's log, but the OS kernel's view. Windows was **re-scanning the UFS drive** (a routine "are you still there?" check), which sends a simple INQUIRY command and waits. The chip never answered: that thread sat for tens of seconds, other work piled up behind it (including a system-wide lock), and the whole machine froze. The drive was also caught **flapping** — repeatedly detected, re-checked, detected again. This is very likely the **same M-PHY relink failure** seen in the storage-driver log, just observed from the PnP/enumeration side instead of the SCSI-command side — Windows re-scanning the bus (INQUIRY) hits the identical "link won't come back" wall that a retried READ does. The thread doesn't tie the two views to one literal event, but they share the same failure class — this is not an independent, unexplained third problem.

**Both problems are root-caused, not open** — the failure is always "the UFS chip stops answering something Windows is waiting on," and it takes two things acting in sequence to turn that into a visible hang: **(1)** a config bug (`FeatureFlags` completion-method + Auto-Hibernate) that makes the original command time out in the first place, fixed by the doorbell-completion default (`0x11`, 25H2'7D); and **(2)** a vendor-dependent gap in how Windows recovers from that timeout, which only SK hynix falls into because its link reports "still up" after an endpoint reset, addressed by a driver change that **skips the broken Device Reset step** (moving to the generic reset path, rolling out via the **25H2'8D CFR**) so recovery reaches Bus Reset's clean HCE-toggle re-init. Fix (1) stops the timeout from happening; fix (2) stops it from turning into a hang on the rare occasions it still does. While those fixes land and roll out via CFR, a **temporary errata (#288262)** — later extended +90 days — plus an **HLK waiver (CSS `16029798734`)** kept certification unblocked. Note that *this sighting itself* closed (Feb 2026) with Issue #2 root-caused and Issue #1 still under HW debug; the FeatureFlags root-cause/fix for Issue #1 was concluded later on the sibling tracker `15019125953`.
